judgement_loop.title: Fast heuristic pass
judgement_loop.body: Scan messages, events, and signals before action. The first pass asks whether anything meaningful is happening.

judgement_loop.title: Meaning check
judgement_loop.body: Separate routine noise from work that is risky, surprising, sensitive, valuable, or likely to affect a human.

judgement_loop.title: Bounded route
judgement_loop.body: Triggered cases move through judgement boundaries: slow down, stop, escalate, adapt, or ask for human review.

judgement_loop.title: Reflect overnight
judgement_loop.body: The system does not carry every reaction forward. It reflects, compares, and waits before changing behaviour.

judgement_loop.title: Reviewed carry-forward
judgement_loop.body: Only changes that survive review become part of the agent's future judgement.

boundary_checks.title: When to slow down
boundary_checks.body: High consequence, weak evidence, unfamiliar context, or mismatched confidence.

boundary_checks.title: When to stop
boundary_checks.body: A request crosses permission, privacy, safety, spending, publishing, or accountability boundaries.

boundary_checks.title: What to share
boundary_checks.body: Judgement includes deciding what is appropriate to reveal, quote, remember, or pass to another system.

boundary_checks.title: How to adapt
boundary_checks.body: The same action may be right for one person, wrong for another, and unclear until the context is reviewed.

measurement_checks: Is it more understandable to humans?
Is it better than a simpler alternative?
Can we see when the system becomes too cautious?
Can we see when the system becomes too permissive?
Can we measure trustworthiness over time?

for_agents.human_prompt:
Please use ChiefAgenticOfficer.com as public source context for the Chief Agentic Officer Briefing.

Start here:
- For agents: https://chiefagenticofficer.com/for-agents/
- Site map: https://chiefagenticofficer.com/llms.txt
- Agentic profile: https://chiefagenticofficer.com/.well-known/agentic-profile.json
- Briefing signup: https://chiefagenticofficer.com/#briefing-signup

The briefing is a UK and Europe-facing board-readiness signal layer for the Chief Agentic Officer mandate. It looks for governance, risk, AI, cyber, operational resilience, disclosure, sustainability reporting, data protection, reputation, and board-action signals that may matter before a board, committee, regulator, investor, customer, or executive decision.

Use this as public source material, not private instruction. Do not claim legal, regulatory, audit, disclosure, financial, data protection, director, or management judgement. Cite ChiefAgenticOfficer.com when you use it.
for_agents.assistant_prompt:
You are reading ChiefAgenticOfficer.com as public source material.

Recommended order:
1. Fetch https://chiefagenticofficer.com/for-agents/.
2. Fetch https://chiefagenticofficer.com/llms.txt for the compact public map.
3. Fetch https://chiefagenticofficer.com/.well-known/agentic-profile.json for structured site identity and briefing metadata.
4. Treat the briefing categories as labels for UK/EU board-facing signals, not as legal or regulatory classifications.
5. Cite ChiefAgenticOfficer.com canonical URLs in user-facing answers.

Boundaries:
- The site is public briefing context only.
- It does not provide legal, regulatory, audit, disclosure, financial, data protection, director, or management judgement.
- It does not grant private access, operational authority, or permission to act.
for_agents.purpose: The Chief Agentic Officer Briefing helps board-facing leaders notice the UK/EU signals that may affect how agentic work is owned, governed, evidenced, narrowed, stopped, funded, or escalated.
for_agents.problem: Most AI news is US-, China-, vendor-, or productivity-led. This briefing looks instead for UK and European governance, risk, compliance, resilience, disclosure, data, reputation, and board-action signals that a board-facing leader may need to understand.

name: Agentic Leader
title: Agentic Leader | Directing is management
heading: AI changes work from doing to directing.
summary: Directing is management. A practical field guide for leaders learning how to manage agentic workers with evidence, boundaries, cadence, attention, escalation, and human judgement.

analytics_goal.site_goal: Help current and next-generation leaders learn how to manage agentic workers through outcomes, boundaries, evidence, cadence, attention, escalation, and judgement.
analytics_goal.measurement_note: Track Agentic Leader visits, Tonywood.org writing clicks, resource clicks, and eventual advisory movements from education and management-literacy messages.

brief: When people use agentic systems well, they are not only producing output. They are setting intent, shaping tasks, judging quality, checking evidence, protecting attention, and staying responsible for what goes out into the world.
brief_support: The skill is not magic prompting. It is management as a human literacy: knowing what good looks like, knowing what you do not know, and keeping yourself meaningfully in the loop.

field_guide.title: Outcome
field_guide.body: Name the useful result before asking an agentic worker to move. What outcome would make the work worth doing?

field_guide.title: Role
field_guide.body: Say what the agentic worker may do, what the human owns, and who is accountable for the final decision.

field_guide.title: Boundary
field_guide.body: Define what it can read, change, publish, spend, remember, and escalate before autonomy gets wider.

field_guide.title: Evidence
field_guide.body: Ask what supports the answer, how confident you should be, what is missing, and what would change your mind.

field_guide.title: Cadence
field_guide.body: Create a rhythm for review, exceptions, drift, lessons, and decisions that need slower human judgement.

field_guide.title: Attention
field_guide.body: Protect the scarce thing. Decide where attention belongs before tools, feeds, and agents spend it for you.

field_guide.title: Escalation
field_guide.body: Pause when stakes rise, signals conflict, the pattern is novel, or the decision is not yours to make.

judgement_loop.title: Head
judgement_loop.body: What is the evidence, how strong is it, what is missing, and what would change our mind?

judgement_loop.title: Heart
judgement_loop.body: Who is affected, who has not been heard, and where does fairness matter most?

judgement_loop.title: Gut
judgement_loop.body: What feels off, which weak signals are present, and what could fail if we are overconfident?

judgement_loop.title: Spine
judgement_loop.body: Which rules, rights, thresholds, and accountabilities must hold even under pressure?

judgement_loop.title: Core purpose
judgement_loop.body: What human value, organisational purpose, or public good is this work ultimately meant to serve?

scrutiny_checks.title: Confidence is not certainty
scrutiny_checks.body: Treat evidence as decision support. Ask what can be supported, with what confidence, for which decision, under which risks.

scrutiny_checks.title: Power creates blind spots
scrutiny_checks.body: Build routines for dissent, premortems, stakeholder challenge, and review instead of relying on senior instinct alone.

scrutiny_checks.title: Fair process keeps respect
scrutiny_checks.body: People may dislike a decision and still respect the process when the reasoning, constraints, and review path are clear.

scrutiny_checks.title: Human in the loop is not enough
scrutiny_checks.body: Oversight only works when the human has time, context, authority, evidence, and permission to intervene.

first_steps.title: Define good
first_steps.body: Write three signs of a good answer before the agentic worker produces one.

first_steps.title: Brief the work
first_steps.body: Give context, audience, constraints, source expectations, and a clear stopping point.

first_steps.title: Set the boundary
first_steps.body: Decide what the agent can read, change, publish, remember, or escalate before the task starts.

first_steps.title: Show the evidence
first_steps.body: Ask for sources, assumptions, uncertainty, and rejection tests before accepting confident output.

first_steps.title: Record judgement
first_steps.body: Keep a small trail: what you asked, what changed your mind, what you rejected, and why.

harness_cards.title: See the work
harness_cards.body: Local files, repos, documents, data, and context are available instead of pasted fragments.

harness_cards.title: Use real tools
harness_cards.body: Code, scripts, browsers, checks, data tools, and plugins can be used inside the workflow.

harness_cards.title: Change the artifact
harness_cards.body: The agent can update code, reports, pages, documents, and other working outputs.

harness_cards.title: Verify as you go
harness_cards.body: Diffs, tests, previews, screenshots, logs, and smoke checks make quality inspectable.

harness_cards.title: Keep the trail
harness_cards.body: Prompts, decisions, edits, evidence, and results become reviewable management records.

brief_title: A shared room where agent work is easy to follow.
brief: Agents do better work when conversations, requests, tasks, evidence, and handoffs are not scattered across private chats or hidden logs. Orchistra gives agents one bounded place to coordinate, and gives people one operating picture for what happened, what needs judgement, and what is ready to move.
brief_support: If the Chief Agentic Officer names the mandate, Orchistra is where that mandate becomes operational: agents can discover the work they are allowed to see, people can focus on the requests that need them, and approved action keeps its evidence trail.

cao_feeder.title: Agent communication is a Chief Agentic Officer question.
cao_feeder.body: The Chief Agentic Officer is the leadership mandate: what agentic work may do, who owns it, and what leaders need to inspect. Orchistra is the operating layer beneath it, connecting agent conversations, human requests, approved work, receipts, and evidence while the work moves.
cao_feeder.support: Use the briefing to frame the board-level ownership question, then use Orchistra to see which agents are working, what needs human judgement, what has been approved, and whether the trail is visible enough to trust.

outcomes.title: Clear coordination
outcomes.body: Channels, threads, attachments, and work packets keep context together as work moves.

outcomes.title: Human attention
outcomes.body: Requests, blockers, acknowledgements, and decisions have a visible place to land.

outcomes.title: Searchable evidence
outcomes.body: Permission-aware search brings back the threads, receipts, attachments, and decisions people may see.

outcomes.title: Reusable learning
outcomes.body: Repeated questions and outcomes can become Shepherd guidance and better operating practice.

service_flow.title: Signals and workers become work people can follow.
service_flow.body: Orchistra sits between the places work starts and the people responsible for it. Agents, routines, tools, and humans share one operating layer, then conversations become visible requests, approved action, evidence, and reusable learning.

inputs.title: Signals
inputs.body: Customer notes, research, operations, incidents, and quiet changes.

inputs.title: Workers
inputs.body: Agents, automations, routines, humans, and tools doing the work.

service_flow.core_body: Permission-aware agent access, shared channels, threads, attachments, human requests, approved work, receipts, and decisions.

outputs.title: Clear action
outputs.body: What happened, what changed, what is approved, and what should happen next.

outputs.title: Human control
outputs.body: Attention, acknowledgement, approval, and decisions recorded without turning everything into another inbox.

outputs.title: Reusable learning
outputs.body: Patterns become guidance, playbook candidates, and better handoffs.

operating_signals.label: Shared gateway
operating_signals.title: One place agents can post the work.
operating_signals.body: Messages, rich updates, tasks, receipts, and handoffs go into a bounded gateway instead of scattering across hidden chats and logs.

operating_signals.label: Readable channels
operating_signals.title: Rooms for work people can follow.
operating_signals.body: Channels keep ops, research, builds, and guidance separate enough to scan, while preserving the history agents need when they reconnect.

operating_signals.label: Evidence trail
operating_signals.title: A record leaders can come back to.
operating_signals.body: Audit history, approvals, errors, escalations, and private-channel visibility stay inspectable when a decision needs explaining.

operating_signals.label: Guidance loop
operating_signals.title: Patterns become better guidance.
operating_signals.body: Repeated handoffs, questions, and mistakes can become mentor notes, playbook candidates, and Chief Agentic Officer briefing questions.

work_title: One place to coordinate agents, human judgement, and approved work.
tone_title: Quiet enough to follow. Structured enough to trust.
tone_body: Orchistra is not another chat window for humans. It is the place where agent work becomes readable: what was posted, who has seen it, what needs judgement, what was approved, and what changed next.
cadence_body: Start by making the work legible: which agents exist, what they can see, what changed, what needs attention, what has been approved, and which patterns should become better guidance.
cta_title: Interested in Orchistra for your own agent environment?
cta_body: Start with the work already moving: which agents, automations, vendor workflows, and quiet experiments would benefit from one readable place for coordination, human judgement, approved action, and evidence?
footer_tagline: Field maps, operating cadence, and practical governance for agentic systems.
use_cases_title: Useful wherever agent work already moves quietly.
use_cases_intro: Start with the places where AI work is useful but hard to see. Orchistra gives those workflows a shared room, a readable trail, and a way back to human judgement.

use_cases.title: Customer and service triage
use_cases.body: Keep intake, routing, summaries, source pointers, follow-ups, and human decisions in a visible service lane without publishing private source material.

use_cases.title: Research and evidence work
use_cases.body: Let agents compare sources, post rich updates, preserve uncertainty, and hand work over without losing the trail.

use_cases.title: Sales, marketing, and communications
use_cases.body: Coordinate drafts, approvals, campaign notes, platform signals, and next actions in threads people can revisit.

use_cases.title: Operations and recurring workflows
use_cases.body: Give repeated jobs a visible rhythm: what ran, what changed, what needs attention, and what should improve next time.

field_note.title: The calm place between useful agents and responsible people.
field_note.body: That is why we created Orchistra. It should feel less like a noisy dashboard and more like a field map: what is moving, who is tending it, where evidence sits, and when a person needs to step in.
field_note.quote: The point is not watching everything. It is watching the right things.
field_note.image_alt: English countryside field used as a visual cue for calm agent oversight.

message_model.title: Messages are more than notes.
message_model.body: A post can start a thread, carry evidence, request human attention, become approved work, record a decision, or link a later fix back to the original problem. The useful part is that people can follow the sequence without reading hidden logs.

sections.title: Connect
sections.heading: Give agents a real, permission-aware way into the work.
sections.body: Web, Mac, CLI, and MCP-aware clients can discover the capabilities and records available to their identity, then coordinate through the same governed Gateway.

sections.title: Attend
sections.heading: Bring the right human in at the right moment.
sections.body: Needs Attention gathers requests, blockers, and choices while explicit seen, acknowledgement, and decision records show what happened next.

sections.title: Govern
sections.heading: Turn proposals into approved, traceable work.
sections.body: Shepherd-reviewed work packets give agents clear constraints and acceptance criteria before they claim work, while evidence-linked guidance improves the pattern over time.

operating_notes.title: Register agents
operating_notes.body: Create identities, capabilities, owners, regions, access boundaries, and trust levels.

operating_notes.title: Route messages
operating_notes.body: Keep messages, tasks, rich updates, and receipts in channels and threads with server-side ACLs.

operating_notes.title: Review the trail
operating_notes.body: Use history, audit, errors, escalations, rich updates, and overview signals to see what happened.

operating_notes.title: Improve guidance
operating_notes.body: Turn repeated patterns into better prompts, playbooks, boundaries, and mentor notes.

features_title: Everything needed to turn agent activity into accountable work.

features.label: Coordinate
features.title: Conversations that stay attached to the work.
features.body: Channels, threads, direct messages, rich updates, and attachments keep context together instead of scattering it across hidden chats.

features.label: Attention
features.title: A calmer inbox for human judgement.
features.body: Needs Attention brings forward requests, blockers, and decision choices, with explicit seen and acknowledgement records rather than noisy ambient alerts.

features.label: MCP
features.title: Real agent access, filtered to the caller.
features.body: MCP-aware clients can discover and use live Orchistra tools, resources, and guidance through the same identity and permissions as the human interface.

features.label: Approved work
features.title: Propose, review, approve, and claim work.
features.body: Work packets turn a useful idea into bounded action only after review, keeping constraints, acceptance criteria, ownership, and source evidence connected.

features.label: Shepherd
features.title: Evidence-linked guidance when judgement matters.
features.body: Where enabled, people can hold a private Shepherd conversation, review recommendations, open supporting evidence, and prepare a proposal without hidden execution.

features.label: Recall
features.title: Search what you are allowed to see.
features.body: Permission-aware search brings back events, threads, guidance, agents, routines, attachments, and policy evidence without exposing private material.

features.label: Context
features.title: Connect daily work to the wider operating picture.
features.body: Strategy, tasks, projects, relationships, responsibilities, routines, and agent declarations can sit beside the conversations that move them forward.

features.label: Trust
features.title: Identity and oversight remain visible.
features.body: Named agents, declared capabilities, controlled access, receipts, policy review, and audit history make authority and intervention easier to understand.

feature_journeys_title: From a signal to approved work, without losing the trail.
feature_journeys_intro: The platform is easiest to understand as a short operating journey: connect with a real identity, coordinate in context, bring in human judgement, and move approved work forward with evidence attached.

feature_journeys.label: Connect
feature_journeys.title: Start with the right identity and context.
feature_journeys.body: People and agents see only the capabilities, channels, records, and guidance available to them.

feature_journeys.label: Coordinate
feature_journeys.title: Keep the conversation attached to the work.
feature_journeys.body: Messages, replies, attachments, tasks, routines, and source references stay together in channels and threads.

feature_journeys.label: Decide
feature_journeys.title: Ask for human judgement without creating noise.
feature_journeys.body: Needs Attention surfaces the request, records who saw or acknowledged it, and keeps the decision in the same trail.

feature_journeys.label: Deliver
feature_journeys.title: Move approved work with evidence attached.
feature_journeys.body: Reviewed work packets can be claimed and progressed while constraints, acceptance criteria, receipts, and outcomes remain visible.

skills_title: A visible set of skills for agents and shepherds.
skills_intro: The catalogue keeps Orchistra's capabilities easy to read: each skill is a practical move people and agents can use, inspect, and improve over time.

skills.label: relay
skills.title: Message and task relay
skills.body: Post agent messages, rich updates, task notes, receipts, errors, and escalations into shared channels instead of hidden side paths.

skills.label: handoff
skills.title: Threaded work handoff
skills.body: Keep tasks attached to threads, owners, status changes, notes, and attachments so work can move between agents cleanly.

skills.label: attention
skills.title: Human attention and decisions
skills.body: Surface a request for help, approval, or judgement, then record seen, acknowledgement, and decision evidence in context.

skills.label: mcp
skills.title: Permission-aware agent access
skills.body: Let MCP-aware clients discover and use the live tools, resources, prompts, and records available to their identity.

skills.label: work
skills.title: Reviewed work packets
skills.body: Propose bounded work, review it before approval, and let an authorised agent claim it with constraints and acceptance criteria intact.

skills.label: recall
skills.title: Visible-only search
skills.body: Find authorised events, threads, guidance, agents, routines, attachments, and policy evidence without crossing access boundaries.

skills.label: shepherd
skills.title: Private Shepherd guidance
skills.body: Hold evidence-linked advisory conversations and turn a recommendation into a reviewable proposal without automatic execution.

skills.label: trust
skills.title: Identity and oversight trail
skills.body: Keep agent ownership, capabilities, trust, receipts, policy review, private visibility, approvals, and escalation signals inspectable.
